title: The present perfect
subtitle: The past that still matters now
review: Written by Claude in the format of the French tense pages. Check the examples and the level.
intro: It joins the **past** to **now**. Something happened before now, but **when** is not important: the important thing is the **result now**, or your **experience**, or that it is **still true**. Never use it with a finished time such as *yesterday*.

blocks.label: Experience
blocks.title: In your life, up to now: ever, never

examples.fr: He **has read** that book three times.

blocks.label: Result now
blocks.title: Something happened, and you can see or feel it now

examples.en: I can't open the door now.
It is in a cast now.

blocks.label: Still true
blocks.title: It started in the past and continues: for, since

examples.fr: I **have lived** here for ten years.
We **have been** friends for a long time.
He **has had** that bike since he was six.

blocks.label: Just, already, yet
blocks.title: News, and things you are waiting for
Pattern
blocks.note: For regular verbs the past participle is the **-ed** form: *played, finished, lived*. For irregular verbs it is the **third form**: *go, went, **gone***.

blocks.title: For or since? Been or gone?
points: **for** + how long: *for two hours, for ten years, for a long time*.
**since** + the starting point: *since Monday, since 2020, since I was a child*.
*She has **gone** to Yangon*: she is there now, or on the way.
*She has **been** to Yangon*: she went and came back. It is her experience.

blocks.text: ever, never, just, already, yet, for, since, before, so far, up to now, today, this week / year (when it is not over), recently, How long …?

examples.en: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.

examples.fr: **Present perfect**: no time, it matters now. *I have seen that film.*
**Past simple**: a finished time. *I saw that film last week.*
**Present perfect**: still true. *She has lived here for five years.*
**Past simple**: finished. *She lived here for five years.*
examples.en: She does not live here now.

examples.fr: **In a conversation**: *“Have you ever been to Bagan?” “Yes, I went there in 2022.”*
examples.en: First the experience (perfect), then the details (past simple).
